title: Bank Capital and Loan Quality Update
subtitle: Summary of key financial metrics and risk factors

overview.text: The bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio stood at 13.2%, which exceeds the regulatory minimum requirement of 10.5% [F1, F2]. This indicates the bank maintains a capital buffer above the mandatory threshold. Additionally, customer deposits were reported at USD 900 million [F5].

Loan quality has shown a negative trend. The nonperforming loan ratio increased to 2.8%, up from 2.1% as of 31 December 2024 [F3, F4]. Management attributed this rise to higher defaults among commercial property borrowers [F6].

highlights.text: CET1 capital ratio of 13.2% is above the 10.5% regulatory minimum [F1, F2].
Nonperforming loan ratio rose to 2.8% from 2.1% at 31 December 2024 [F3, F4].
Management cited higher defaults among commercial property borrowers as the driver for the increase in nonperforming loans [F6].

risks.text: Rising nonperforming loans due to higher defaults among commercial property borrowers [F6].
Increase in nonperforming loan ratio from 2.1% to 2.8% indicates deteriorating asset quality [F3, F4].
